name: Theologist Scholar Archetype
body:
Associated Skill Knowledge (religion) (Int)

Basic Study Ability
Religious Theory (Ex)

Choose one domain or inquisition available to a cleric or inquisitor. You gain the 1st-level abilities granted by that domain or inquisition, using your ranks in Knowledge (religion) as your effective cleric or inquisitor level, as appropriate.

Associated Technique n/a (There is no technique associated with the Theology study.)

Advanced Study Abilities
Channel Energy (Su)

Prerequisite(s): Religious Theory study ability, scholar level 5th.

You can channel energy as a cleric of a level equal to your ranks in Knowledge (religion).

If your alignment is good, you channel positive energy; if it is evil, you channel negative energy. If you are neutral, you decide when you first gain this study ability whether to channel positive or negative energy; once this decision has been made, it cannot be changed. You can use this ability a maximum number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier, and each use expends 2 points of inspiration.

Scholarly Prayers I

Prerequisite(s): Intelligence 10, Wisdom 10, Religious Theory study ability, scholar level 2nd.

Your diligent study of religion has allowed you to acquire an understanding of divine magic. You can prepare a limited number of divine spells per day. You do not gain domain spells. All 0-level cleric spells are considered to be on your spell list. You can prepare one orison per day, plus one additional orison for every 4 ranks you possess in Knowledge (religion). Each morning, you prepare these orisons just as a cleric. However, you use Intelligence as your casting statistic. Casting any prepared orison requires the expenditure of 1 point of inspiration. Your caster level for these spells is equal to your ranks in Knowledge (religion), and the DC for a saving throw against any of them is 10 + the spell level + your INT modifier. You can use either a holy symbol or a scholarly tome (such as your scholar’s notebook) as a divine focus for any spell that calls for one.

Scholarly Prayers II

Prerequisite(s): Intelligence 12, Wisdom 12, Scholarly Prayers I study ability, scholar level 3rd.

You gain one 1st-level spell slot, and all 1st-level cleric spells are considered to be on your spell list. At 6th level, you gain one 2nd-level spell slot, and all 2d-level cleric spells are considered to be on your spell list.

You gain additional 1st-level spell slots when you reach 8 and 14 ranks in Knowledge (religion). You do not gain bonus spell slots for high ability scores. Each morning, you prepare spells in these slots, just as a cleric. Casting any prepared orison no longer requires inspiration, but casting a 1st- or 2nd-level spell requires the expenditure of 1 point of inspiration (in addition to the appropriate 1st- or 2nd-level spell slot). This otherwise follows the rules for the Scholarly Prayers I study ability.

Scholarly Prayers III

Prerequisite(s): Intelligence 14, Wisdom 14, Scholarly Prayers II study ability scholar level 9th.

You gain one 3rd-level spell slot, and all 3rd-level cleric spells are considered to be on your spell list. When you reach 12 ranks in Knowledge (religion), you gain an additional 2nd-level spell slot. When you reach 15 ranks in Knowledge (religion), you gain one 4th-level spell slot and all 4th-level cleric spells are considered to be on your spell list.

Casting any prepared 1st- or 2nd-level spell no longer requires inspiration, but casting a 3rd- or 4th-level spell requires the expenditure of 1 point of inspiration (in addition to the appropriate spell slot). This otherwise follows the rules for the Scholarly Prayers I study ability.
